951.event_title: Princess Alice of Battenberg hides the Cohen family in occupied Athens
951.event: Princess Alice of Battenberg, mother of Prince Philip and a member of the Greek royal family by marriage, had known the family of Haimaki Cohen, a former Greek member of parliament, before the war. After German forces took control of Athens in September 1943, she took his widow Rachel Cohen and some of her children into her own residence and hid them there until the city was liberated, answering questions from the Gestapo without giving them away. She never spoke of it; her children learned of it only later, and in 1993 Yad Vashem recognised her as Righteous Among the Nations.
951.explanation: Alice's rescue combined uprightness in a time of danger with a modesty so complete that her own family did not know what she had done.
951.tie_back: The kural says rectitude and a sense of shame, found together as second nature, mark those of good family, and Alice did right quietly and never sought credit for it.
951._accuracy_note: Reasonable fit: rectitude and modesty appear together in a person of royal lineage, though the kural's specific virtue of impartiality is only partly shown.

952.event_title: John Quincy Adams returns to Congress after his presidency
952.event: John Quincy Adams, son of the second American president John Adams, was elected to the House of Representatives in 1830 after his own single term as president and served there until his death. For years he fought the House's gag rule, which tabled without debate all petitions against slavery, until it was repealed in 1844. On 21 February 1848 he collapsed at his desk in the House chamber and died in the Capitol two days later.
952.explanation: Adams accepted a lesser office and spent his last seventeen years steadily pressing an unpopular principle, showing a consistency of conduct that did not depend on rank.
952.tie_back: The kural says those of good family never slip from right conduct, truthfulness and shame over a lifetime, and Adams kept to his course until the day he fell at his post.
952._accuracy_note: Next-best: the event shows lifelong steadiness in someone from a distinguished family, but it does not directly show truthfulness or shame as the kural names them.

953.event_title: The Maharaja of Travancore issues the Temple Entry Proclamation
953.event: On 12 November 1936 Maharaja Chithira Thirunal Balarama Varma of Travancore issued a proclamation opening the temples under his government to all Hindus, removing the ban that had kept people of the so-called lower castes out of them. The proclamation followed years of campaigning, including the Vaikom Satyagraha of 1924-25. It was hailed as one of the first measures of its kind in India, and the Government of Kerala still marks its anniversary.
953.explanation: A ruler of an old royal house used his authority to end a practice of exclusion, treating all his subjects as equally welcome.
953.tie_back: Among the four marks of a noble family the kural lists generosity and never belittling others, and the proclamation was a royal act against the belittling of a whole section of society.
953._accuracy_note: Reasonable fit to generosity and not scorning others; the kural's cheerful face and kind words are not documented here.

954.event_title: King Albert I of Belgium rejects the German ultimatum
954.event: On 2 August 1914 Germany delivered an ultimatum demanding free passage for its armies across neutral Belgium, offering assurances that Belgium would keep its independence and possessions after the war if it agreed. The Belgian government, meeting under King Albert I, rejected the demand on 3 August, stating that to accept would sacrifice the nation's honour and betray its duty. German forces invaded the next day, and the violation of Belgian neutrality brought Britain into the war.
954.explanation: Belgium chose to defend its pledged neutrality at enormous cost rather than accept a safe bargain that would have dishonoured it.
954.tie_back: The kural says the nobly born will not do a lowering deed even for untold riches, and King Albert would not trade his country's honour for the guarantees Germany offered.
954._accuracy_note: Strong fit to refusing gain at the price of honour, though the inducement was security rather than wealth, and the decision was a national one.

955.event_title: Anna Maria Luisa de' Medici signs the Family Pact
955.place: Florence, Grand Duchy of Tuscany (now Italy)
955.event: When her brother Gian Gastone, the last Medici grand duke, died in 1737 without an heir, the rule of Tuscany passed to Francis Stephen of Lorraine and the Medici dynasty lost its power. Anna Maria Luisa de' Medici, the last member of the family, signed the Family Pact on 31 October 1737, binding the Medici collections of paintings, statues, libraries and other treasures to Florence and forbidding their removal from the city. The pact stated that the works were to remain for the ornament of the state, the use of the public and the attraction of visitors, and it took full effect on her death in 1743.
955.explanation: Thanks to the pact, the core of the Medici collections remains in Florence today, in museums such as the Uffizi and the Pitti Palace.
955.tie_back: The kural says an old family keeps its generous nature even when its power to give has shrunk, and the last Medici, with the dynasty's rule gone, gave its greatest treasures to the public.
955._accuracy_note: Strong fit: a declining ancient family continues its tradition of patronage; the family's reduced standing was political rather than financial poverty.

956.event_title: Helmuth James von Moltke and the Kreisau Circle
956.event: Helmuth James Graf von Moltke, a lawyer from the distinguished Prussian Moltke family, gathered opponents of the Nazi regime from different backgrounds, including on his family estate at Kreisau, to plan the principles of a just order for Germany after Nazism. He was arrested in January 1944 for warning a friend of an impending arrest. Tried before the People's Court in January 1945, he was condemned although his part in the July 1944 plot against Hitler could not be proved, and he was executed at Plotzensee prison in Berlin on 23 January 1945.
956.explanation: Moltke refused to accommodate a criminal regime even though his family name and position could have bought him safety.
956.tie_back: The kural says those resolved to live true to a spotless family line will not stoop to unworthy acts, and Moltke held to his principles to the end rather than compromise them.
956._accuracy_note: Reasonable fit to refusing unworthy conduct out of loyalty to principle; the kural's emphasis on deceit and on family line is only partly reflected.

957.event_title: Prince Bernhard of the Netherlands and the Lockheed affair
957.event: In 1976 a senior Lockheed executive told a United States Senate committee that the company had paid money to a very senior Dutch official, and suspicion fell on Prince Bernhard, husband of Queen Juliana. A Dutch government commission reported in August 1976 that there was no firm proof he had taken a bribe, but found that he had been open to dishonourable requests and offers. The prince had to give up his military posts and stop appearing in uniform, and he resigned most of his public roles, though parliament decided against prosecution.
957.explanation: Because of his position at the centre of the royal family, the affair drew attention around the world and damaged the reputation of a once-popular war hero.
957.tie_back: The kural says a fault in someone of high birth is seen by everyone, like the spot on the moon, and the prince's lapse became international news because of who he was.
957._accuracy_note: Strong fit to a high-born person's fault being exposed to all; the commission did not find proof that a bribe was taken, and the entry reflects that.

958.event_title: Lord Ashley carries the Mines Act of 1842
958.event: In 1842 a Royal Commission report on women and children working in British coal mines caused public dismay, and Lord Ashley, heir to the earldom of Shaftesbury, took up their cause in the House of Commons. He went down a coal mine himself to see the conditions, and pressed a bill through Parliament the same year. The Mines Act of 1842 banned women and girls, and boys under ten, from working underground.
958.explanation: Ashley used the standing of an aristocratic family on behalf of people who had no voice in Parliament, and became known as one of the great reformers of the century.
958.tie_back: The kural treats compassion as the mark of good birth whose absence makes people doubt a person's lineage, and Ashley's compassion was what made his nobility respected.
958._accuracy_note: Next-best: the event shows the kural's ideal in reverse (compassion confirming nobility) rather than a lack of love causing doubt about someone's family.

959.event_title: Shaw's Pygmalion has its premiere in Vienna
959.event: George Bernard Shaw's play Pygmalion was first performed at the Hofburg Theatre in Vienna on 16 October 1913, in a German translation by Siegfried Trebitsch, and opened in London in April 1914. Its hero, the phonetics professor Henry Higgins, wagers that by changing the speech of a Cockney flower seller he can pass her off as a duchess. Shaw described it as a play about phonetics, and it became a classic comedy about language and the English class system.
959.explanation: Pygmalion made famous the idea that the way a person speaks immediately reveals their background to others.
959.tie_back: The kural says a person's words show the family they come from as surely as a sprout shows the soil, which is the observation on which Shaw built his whole play.
959._accuracy_note: Reasonable fit: the event is the staging of a fictional play, and Shaw's point that speech can be learned partly cuts against the kural's link between speech and birth.

960.event_title: Emperor Akihito and Empress Michiko kneel to speak with evacuees
960.event: On 10 July 1991, in his first official visit to a disaster area as emperor, Akihito travelled with Empress Michiko to Shimabara after the eruption of Mount Unzen had killed 43 people. At an evacuation shelter the couple knelt on the floor to talk face to face with residents, something scarcely imaginable under earlier emperors, and some people complained that the emperor had been made to kneel. They continued the practice in later disasters, and it became known in Japan as the Heisei style.
960.explanation: The imperial couple's humility toward ordinary people helped bring the monarchy closer to the public and won it wide affection.
960.tie_back: The kural says that if you want a noble family name you must be humble toward everyone, and the emperor of an ancient line kneeling to listen to evacuees showed exactly that.
960._accuracy_note: Strong fit to humility toward all as the keeper of a family's standing; the kural's first clause, about a sense of shame, is not illustrated.
